43711.subject: Chemistry
43711.question_text: If the volume of a gas at 35°C is 60cm\(^3\), what would be its volume in cm\(^3\) at 273k?
43711.explanation:
This problem can be solved using Charles's Law, which states that the volume of a given mass of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature, provided the pressure remains constant.

V\(_1\) = 60cm\(^3\)    T\(_1\) = 35\(^0\)C + 273K = 308K;  V\(_2\) = ?    T\(_2\) = 273K

Applying Charles' law,

  \(\frac{V_1}{T_1}\) = \(\frac{V_2}{T_2}\) 

\(\frac{60}{308}\) = \(\frac{V_2}{273}\) 

V\(_2\) = \(\frac{60  x  273}{308}\)

      = 53.18 cm\(^3\)

43718.subject: Chemistry
43718.question_text: How many zones are present in a luminous Bunsen burner flame?
43718.explanation:
The luminous bunsen burner flame has four zones namely:

  • Dark zone/ zone of unburnt gas; burning of the gas does not take place here, it is dark and cool.
  • Luminous yellow zone; the gas burns in this zone but not completely because of limited air. Tiny particles glow in this region to give out light.
  • Thin outer zone; the zone is colorless and gas burns completely due to plenty of air.
  • Blue zone; this zone receives plenty of air and burning is more complete than in the luminous zone.
